content.title: About
content.content: Bulgur is a whole‑grain product made from pre‑cooked, dried and cracked hard wheat (triticale). It has a light nutty flavor, a slightly chewy texture and cooks quickly because the grain is already partially cooked.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bulgur is a staple in Middle Eastern cuisines, especially Turkish, Lebanese and Armenian.
Unlike couscous, bulgur is not steamed; it is made from whole grain that is boiled, dried and cracked.
It comes in several grinds: fine (for tabbouleh), medium (for salads) and coarse (for soups).
Bulgur is the main ingredient of the classic salad tabbouleh, mixed with parsley, tomatoes and mint.
Because the bran is retained, bulgur preserves most of the fiber and vitamins of the original wheat.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety and helps regulate blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Complex carbohydrates provide sustained energy, making bulgur a good choice for athletes and active individuals.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B3 and B6 contribute to energy metabolism and nervous‑system health.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: Bulgur supplies iron, magnesium, phosphorus and zinc, important for blood formation, bones and immunity.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Its low fat content makes bulgur suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Bulgur is made from wheat, so it is not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking before cooking lowers its level.

items.title: Food allergies
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to wheat.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bulgur can be used as a side dish, added to salads (tabbouleh), soups, stuffed vegetables or incorporated into vegetarian patties. To cook, pour boiling water over the grain in a 1:2 ratio, cover and let stand 10–15 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bulgur in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For storage longer than six months, keep it in the refrigerator to prevent insect infestation.
